name: Gulf Oil Lubricants India Ltd
title: Gulf Oil Lubricants India Ltd - 538567 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Volume-led Q1 FY27: core lube volume +17% YoY to 48,000 KL and revenue +33% to INR 1,320 cr, but margin held ~13% only via pass-through; full cost pass-through lands in Q2/Q3 while base oil stays tight.

utilisation.quote: our capacity is in full stream, no problem

capex.quote: Chennai is on track. Silvassa, we are also expecting that some of the augmented production will start and that also should be there by financial year end.

triggers.label: Multiple B2C price hikes in quarter
triggers.quote: we have seen close to 3 increases, which has happened starting March end, April beginning, which is practically every month or so

triggers.label: Capacity expansion ~70% by FY-end
triggers.quote: Silvassa and Chennai, as we announced 70% increase in capacity

triggers.label: Margin per litre protected, % diluted
triggers.quote: The percentage margins are slightly dilutive in these kinds of inflationary environment

triggers.label: Inventory build INR 108-109 cr
triggers.quote: our inventory has gone up by INR108 crores this quarter at the end of the quarter

guidance.value: 2x to 3x industry growth, double-digit value growth
guidance.quote: we will continue to grow 2 to 3x the market with the EBITDA band, which we will try to maintain in the range of 12% to 14%
on a long -term sustainable basis, yes, our 12% to 14% guided band is still intact
take the EV business as per our earlier guidance in the range of around INR300 crores to INR400 crores in 3 to 4 years

guidance.quote: Chennai is on track. Silvassa, we are also expecting that some of the augmented production will start

we normally would not like to give that detail because it's a large part of us is related to contracts
we don't calculate gross margins on a daily basis

summary.headline: Gulf Oil Q1 FY27 revenue rose 33% to INR 1,320 crore and EBITDA 35% to INR 170 crore, with lubes volume up 17% to 48,000 KL.

financial_highlights.change: Highest ever; no YoY figure stated
Inventory up INR 108 crore QoQ per analyst; management attributed to valuation rise, not gains

segments.name: B2C (retail/channel)
segments.commentary: Grew double digits; PCMO (passenger car) led, with gains in agriculture, commercial vehicles and motorcycles. Around 55% of sales mix.

segments.name: OEM
segments.commentary: Double-digit growth; agriculture (Mahindra, Swaraj) in franchisee workshops and motorcycles (Bajaj) led. Around 45% B2B combined with B2B.

segments.name: B2B (industry, infra, mining)
segments.commentary: Growth across customer base with new customer acquisitions in infra; combined B2B share about 45% of sales. Marine also grew double digit.

segments.name: AdBlue
segments.commentary: 40,000 KL in Q1; top-3 supplier in India; low realisation with single-digit margin, guided to mid-single-digit margin going forward.

segments.name: Tirex (EV DC/AC chargers)
segments.commentary: Q1 subdued as e-bus depot orders slowed; management expects H1 revenue positive with most growth in Q2 and Q3. Holds 8-10% share in DC charger business per management.

qa_highlights.question: Is Q1 volume growth partly anticipatory buying, and how will it normalise in Q2-Q3?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said supply security drove some stocking; industry grew 3-4%, and Gulf expects to keep 2-3x industry growth. Monsoon quarter Jul-Sep is seasonally softer for B2C, but OEM buying continues.

qa_highlights.question: Has EBITDA margin guidance of 12-14% been revisited given per-litre EBITDA rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Manish said percentage margins are diluted in inflation; per-litre margin is the priority. The 12-14% band is still intact on a long-term basis, with 14-16% targeted via premiumisation.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any inventory gain in margins?
qa_highlights.answer: No. The company uses weighted-average costing and does not play on inventory; pass-through is immediate in theory, with timing lags.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook on base oil supply and cost into July-August?
qa_highlights.answer: Base oil has not eased with crude; Hormuz is still almost shut. Company has long-term refiner tie-ups plus spot sourcing and 30-45 days base oil inventory; prices reviewed monthly.

qa_highlights.question: Operating expense fall of ~190 bps as share of revenue: drivers, and A&P?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said A&P is still around 3% of revenue, not cut significantly; savings came from fixed-cost absorption and other optimisation. Absolute A&P in rupees not disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Tirex: CPO plans and competitive landscape?
qa_highlights.answer: Tirex is not in CPO business; it manufactures chargers for charge point manufacturers. CPO entry evaluated at an appropriate time, not near term.

guidance_outlook: Volume growth guided at 2-3x industry growth (industry ~3-4%), i.e., roughly double-digit volume growth; management says Q1 17% growth was higher than normal.
EBITDA margin band of 12-14% reiterated on a long-term basis; per-litre EBITDA is the primary focus during inflation; medium-term move to 14-16% band linked to premiumisation.
Full price-increase reflection expected in Q2 or Q3 as pipeline inventory clears; B2C pricing takes 1-2 months to fully flow through.
Silvassa and Chennai capacity expansion (70% increase) phased: Chennai on track for Q3 (December), Silvassa augmented production by FY-end (March 2027).
EV business guided at INR 300-400 crore in 3-4 years, dependent on e-bus tenders materialising over next 1-2 years.
Monsoon quarter (Jul-Sep) expected to be seasonally softer for B2C but management expects a positive, good-growth quarter; July described as normal.
capex_capacity: Silvassa and Chennai expansion, announced as 70% capacity increase; phased commissioning in Q3 and Q4. Chennai on track (by December); Silvassa augmented output expected by financial year end.
Tirex moving to a new, upgraded plant to increase capacity; management says capacity should cover INR 300-400 crore revenue ambition.
Base oil inventory held for at least 30-45 days; Silvassa plant operating normally with no production impact from local flooding.
demand_pricing: Q1 volume growth 17% YoY vs industry ~3-4%; management attributes part of growth to customers securing supply amid Hormuz disruption (pre-buying/stocking).

Pricing: B2C saw close to three price increases from end-March/April, roughly monthly; B2B repriced in 2-3 staggered stages via formula and negotiation. Another retail price increase effective 1 July.
Base oil prices: crude fell from above $100 to below $85, but base oil prices have not fallen similarly; some grades (Group III, high-end) still rising; others softened in the last month.

Competition: management reports no change in pricing discipline or promotional intensity; price increases industry-wide described as unprecedented. Management states Gulf is taking some pricing leadership in certain B2C products.
Management says it has not seen demand destruction yet; elasticity risk noted at a certain price point, especially motorcycles.
risks_watch: Strait of Hormuz disruption and base oil availability; Group III and high-end base oil prices still rising.
Full price pass-through lag: Q2/Q3 margin depends on pricing actions and possible B2C price rollbacks as costs ease.
Demand elasticity and down-trading in B2C if unprecedented price increases persist, especially motorcycles.
Monsoon-season softness in Jul-Sep; sustainability of 17% volume growth after supply-security stocking.
Tirex execution: e-bus tender timing and H1/Q2 revenue ramp; EV revenue target depends on tenders in next 1-2 years.
Inventory built up (about INR 108-109 crore per analyst) and its valuation effect on reported margins.
key_quotes: We've been able to keep the margin at 13%, which is within the guided range.
So, we would term it as a volume-led profitable growth for the quarter is what we have been able to achieve with a lot of emphasis on the supply security.
We would say Strait of Hormuz is still like almost shut. So it's very difficult to say how the things will move.
Gulf has done very well. We've been able to get whatever we gauge.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on volume, record revenue and supply resilience, but noticeably cautious on margins and pricing, with repeated caveats that percentage margins are unreliable during this inflationary, fluid base oil environment.

adds.what: Chennai lubes capacity expansion (part of 70% total increase with Silvassa)
Silvassa lubes capacity expansion (augmented production, part of 70% total increase)
Tirex upgraded EV charger plant to increase capacity

growth.why: Management guides core lube volume growth at 2-3x industry (~3-4%), i.e. roughly double-digit, with a phased ~70% capacity increase (Chennai by December, Silvassa by March 2027), though Q1's 17% volume growth was called above normal and partly pre-buying amid Hormuz disruption.
